narrative.intro: AMI Metals has $2B in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. The company received 9 awards with an average award size of $225M. Obligations are up 4136383.9% year over year. The Department of Homeland Security is the dominant buyer, accounting for $2B in obligations. The Department of Defense appears as a secondary buyer with $13.5K in obligations. Process, Physical Distribution, and Logistics Consulting Services is the largest NAICS market for AMI Metals at $2B. Other Support Activities for Air Transportation is listed with $13.5K. Historical obligations through prior fiscal years are small by comparison: FY21 shows $9.8K, FY22 shows $165K, FY23 shows $109K, FY24 shows $346K, and FY25 shows $48.9K. The current-year totals are partial because the data are fiscal year to date. The note clarifies that figures are contract obligations except award-value figures in certain tables, which are total contract values. These figures show a sharp concentration of FY2026 obligations in a single agency and a single NAICS market.

sections.heading: Who are AMI Metals biggest federal buyers?
sections.body: The Department of Homeland Security obligated $2B to AMI Metals in FY2026 to date. The Department of Defense obligated $13.5K. Those two agencies are the only buyers listed among the top buying agencies for FY2026 to date.

sections.heading: How concentrated are AMI Metals obligations by market and fiscal year?
sections.body: Process, Physical Distribution, and Logistics Consulting Services accounts for $2B of AMI Metals obligations in FY2026 to date.
